nodes.description: Address of the contract owner; initialized to msg.sender and used by the onlyBy(owner) access-control modifier and as recipient of funds.
Dynamic array of players; pushed on buy-in, indexed to pick a winner, and reset to length 0 after payout/refund.
Pseudo-random seed derived from previous seed, last player and block.timestamp; used as the randomness source for the lottery.
Fixed payout amount (0.1 ether) transferred to the winner.
Owner-guarded function that reassigns the owner state variable to the supplied address.
Internal pseudo-random generator: mixes playerPool last entry, seed and now (block.timestamp) and returns seed % upper.
Payable entry point; validates msg.value * 10, records msg.sender in playerPool and triggers selectWinner at 11 players.
Private function that picks a winner index via random(), pays the winner and the owner, then empties the pool.
Owner-only payable function that loops over playerPool transferring 100 finney to every player and then resets the pool.
Owner-only function that calls refund() and then selfdestructs the contract, sending remaining balance to owner.
Payable fallback function that mirrors buyIn(): checks msg.value * 10, records the sender and may trigger selectWinner.
msg.sender - untrusted caller address used for ownership, pool membership and modifier checks.
block.timestamp (now) - miner-influenceable value used directly as a randomness input in random().
winner.transfer(amount) - external value transfer to an attacker-controlled address that can reenter the contract.
owner.transfer(this.balance) - external value transfer performed before state is fully cleaned up.
playerPool[i].transfer(100 finney) inside a loop - external calls to untrusted players during iteration.
selfdestruct(owner) - irreversibly destroys the contract and sends funds to the owner.
seed = keccak256(keccak256(playerPool[last], seed), now) - weakness: randomness derived from public/block values, predictable and manipulable.
msg.value * 10 comparison - arithmetic on a caller-supplied value used as the bet validation condition.
_newOwner parameter of changeOwner(); becomes the new owner address.
upper parameter of random(); the modulo bound applied to the seed.
Local variable winner in selectWinner() holding the address chosen by random().
Loop counter i used in refund() to iterate over playerPool.

edges.reason: owner state variable is initialized from msg.sender at deployment, coupling ownership to the untrusted caller.
msg.sender is pushed into playerPool inside buyIn().
buyIn() mutates playerPool with playerPool.push(msg.sender).
msg.sender is pushed into playerPool by the fallback function.
fallback() mutates playerPool with playerPool.push(msg.sender).
buyIn() calls selectWinner() once playerPool.length >= 11, entering the payout logic.
fallback() calls selectWinner() once playerPool.length >= 11, entering the payout logic.
selectWinner() invokes random(playerPool.length) to choose the winner index.
upper parameter defines the modulo bound of the returned pseudo-random value.
block.timestamp (now) is read inside random() and mixed into the seed.
block.timestamp is the sole external entropy source of the seed computation, creating timestamp dependency.
the timestamp-based keccak256 computation is written into the seed state variable.
random() stores the newly computed value into the seed state variable.
random() returns the index consumed by selectWinner().
the value returned by random() indexes playerPool and is stored in the local winner variable.
the locally chosen winner address is the recipient of the external transfer.
selectWinner() performs winner.transfer(amount) sending funds to an untrusted address.
selectWinner() performs owner.transfer(this.balance) after the winner payout.
the owner state variable is the recipient of the remaining contract balance.
winner.transfer() invokes the recipient's fallback with 2300 gas before playerPool is reset, enabling reentrancy attempts.
owner.transfer() is an external call executed before state cleanup completes, allowing callback reentry.
selectWinner() resets playerPool.length = 0 after the payouts, so state changes follow external calls.
the loop counter i indexes playerPool, whose element becomes the recipient of the external transfer.
refund() runs a for loop driven by the local counter i over the length of playerPool.
refund() executes playerPool[i].transfer(100 finney) to each untrusted player inside an unbounded loop.
each transfer in the refund loop is an external call that can reenter refund() before playerPool is cleared.
refund() sets playerPool.length = 0 after paying out all players.
close() calls refund() before destroying the contract.
onlyBy(owner) restricts refund() to the owner address.
onlyBy(owner) restricts close() to the owner address.
onlyBy(owner) restricts changeOwner() to the owner address.
msg.sender is compared against owner in the onlyBy modifier guarding changeOwner().
changeOwner() overwrites the privileged owner state variable.
the _newOwner parameter flows directly into the owner state variable.
_newOwner is the argument processed by changeOwner().
close() invokes selfdestruct(owner), irreversibly destroying the contract.
the owner address is passed as the selfdestruct beneficiary inside close().
buyIn() computes msg.value * 10 to validate the exact bet size, an unchecked multiplication.
the fallback performs the same msg.value * 10 arithmetic check.

normalization_plan.reason: _newOwner is a pure input of changeOwner(); its only role is to be assigned into the owner state variable, so it can be folded into the function node.
upper only bounds the modulo inside random(); it carries no independent state and is absorbed by the random() function node.
the local winner variable exists exclusively to hold the recipient of winner.transfer(amount), so it merges into that unsafe external-transfer operation.
the loop counter i is only used to index playerPool for the per-player transfer inside refund(), so it merges into the unsafe refund transfer operation.
